title: UEFI firmware self-identifies as EDK II (OVMF) in SystemBiosVersion, contradicting the claimed AMI/MSI board
evidence: SystemBiosVersion : {ALASKA - 1, A.32, EDK II - 10000}
bare_metal: An MSI PRO B650-A WIFI (MS-7D75) ships AMI AptioV. Its SystemBiosVersion would list only the AMI strings (e.g. 'ALASKA - 1', 'A.32') and never 'EDK II - 10000'. 'EDK II' is the TianoCore reference implementation that QEMU uses via OVMF; the '10000' build tag is OVMF's. SMBIOS/BIOS strings were otherwise rewritten to impersonate the MSI board, but this third entry is pulled from the live firmware vendor string and was missed. Confidence: high
repro: reg query "HKLM\HARDWARE\DESCRIPTION\System" /v SystemBiosVersion

title: ACPI DSDT contains QEMU's literal hotplug/GPE container device names
command: Get-WmiObject Win32_PnPEntity | Where-Object {$_.DeviceID -match "^ACPI"} | Select-Object -ExpandProperty DeviceID | Sort-Object
evidence:
ACPI\PNP0A06\CPU_HOTPLUG_RESOURCES
ACPI\PNP0A06\GPE0_RESOURCES
ACPI\PNP0A06\PCI_HOTPLUG_RESOURCES
ACPI\PNP0A06\SMI_RESOURCES
bare_metal: A real AMI AptioV DSDT has no PNP0A06 generic-container stubs with these names. These four _HID/PNP0A06 containers are emitted verbatim by QEMU's ACPI table generator (hw/i386/acpi-build.c) to reserve I/O windows for CPU hotplug, the GPE0 block, PCI hotplug and the SMI command port. The ACPI OEM IDs were rewritten to ALASKA/'A M I' to hide BOCHS/BXPC, but the device names inside the DSDT body were not. Confidence: high
repro: pnputil /enum-devices | findstr /i HOTPLUG_RESOURCES   (or the WMI query above)

title: Boot SSD advertises 'Samsung SSD 990 PRO 2TB' but reports exactly 256 GiB
evidence:
FriendlyName    : Samsung SSD 990 PRO 2TB
SerialNumber    : S73WNJ0X281324I     _00000001.
Size            : 274877906944
BusType         : NVMe
FirmwareVersion : 4B2QJXD7
bare_metal: A genuine Samsung 990 PRO 2TB reports 2,000,398,934,016 bytes. Here the model string says 2TB while the capacity is 274,877,906,944 = exactly 256 x 2^30. Real SSD capacities are decimal-rounded and never land on an exact binary power; an exact GiB multiple is the signature of a host-side backing image given a size in GiB. The model/firmware strings were set to impersonate a 990 PRO but the backing file's real size shows through. The serial also carries QEMU's space padding to 20 bytes plus a '_00000001.' title: CPUID reports no MONITOR/MWAIT, no PCID, and no Core Performance Boost on a CPU identifying as Ryzen 5 9600X
command: Raw CPUID via a VirtualAlloc'd x64 stub (cpuid with leaf in eax, results written to a uint[4]); leaves 1 and 0x80000007 decoded
evidence:
Brand string: 'AMD Ryzen 5 9600X 6-Core Processor'
Leaf 1: EAX=0x00B40F40 ECX=0x7FF83203 EDX=0x178BFBFF
  bit3  MONITOR/MWAIT    = 0
  bit17 PCID             = 0
  bit31 HYPERVISOR       = 0
Leaf 0x80000007 EDX=0x00000100  InvariantTSC(bit8)=1  CPB/Boost(bit9)=0  EffFreq(bit10)=0
bare_metal: A real Ryzen 5 9600X (Zen 5, family 0x1A model 0x44) sets CPUID.1:ECX[3] MONITOR, CPUID.1:ECX[17] PCID, CPUID.80000007:EDX[9] CPB (Core Performance Boost) and EDX[10] EffFreq (the APERF/MPERF pair). CPB is how the 3.9 GHz base / 5.4 GHz boost on this part is advertised - no shipping Ryzen clears it. MONITOR/MWAIT and PCID are both routinely masked off by hypervisors (MWAIT cannot be exposed without host core pinning), and CPB/EffFreq are meaningless to a vCPU, so all four are absent here. Consistent with this: WMI MaxClockSpeed reports 4400 MHz, which is neither the 9600X's 3900 base nor its 5400 boost. CPUID.1:ECX[31] has been deliberately cleared and leaf 0x40000000 zeroed to hide the hypervisor, so the masked feature set is the remaining tell. Confidence: high
repro: Any CPUID tool: check CPUID.1:ECX bits 3 and 17 and CPUID.80000007:EDX bit 9 against the brand string in CPUID.80000002-4

title: CPUID takes ~1037 cycles - an unconditional VM exit (bare metal is ~1-2 orders of magnitude cheaper)
command: RDTSC-bracketed loop of 20000 'xor eax,eax; cpuid' vs 20000 'xor eax,eax; nop; nop', best of 7 runs, via a VirtualAlloc'd x64 stub
evidence:
CPUID loop: 20743652 cycles / 20000 iters = 1,037.2 cyc/CPUID
NOP   loop: 16280 cycles / 20000 iters = 0.8 cyc/iter
Ratio CPUID/NOP = 1,274.2x
bare_metal: On a bare-metal Zen 5, CPUID leaf 0 is serializing but handled entirely in the core: roughly 40-150 cycles. CPUID is unconditionally intercepted by AMD-V, so every execution here costs a world switch to the hypervisor and back - the ~1000-cycle figure is the VMEXIT/VMRUN round trip, and it persists even though the hypervisor bit and the 0x4xxxxxxx leaves have been hidden. The invariant-TSC bit is set and the TSC is not being scaled, so this timing is directly comparable. Confidence: high that >=500 cyc/CPUID implies virtualisation; medium that the exact figure is reproducible across hosts
repro: Time CPUID in an RDTSC-bracketed loop; compare against a non-trapping serializing baseline. >500 cycles per CPUID means an intercept.

title: Two ACPI tables still carry OVMF's INTEL/EDK2 header IDs while the rest were rewritten to AMI
command: GetSystemFirmwareTable('ACPI', <sig>) via P/Invoke; OEMID at offset 10, OEMTableID at 16, Creator at 28
evidence:
FACP  len=244    rev=3  OEMID='ALASKA'  OEMTableID='A M I   '  Creator='INTL'
APIC  len=208    rev=3  OEMID='ALASKA'  OEMTableID='A M I   '  Creator='INTL'
SSDT  len=72     rev=2  OEMID='ALASKA'  OEMTableID='A M I   '  Creator='INTL'  CreatorRev=0x20260408
WSMT  len=40     rev=1  OEMID='INTEL '  OEMTableID='EDK2    '  Creator='    '  CreatorRev=0x1000013
BGRT  len=56     rev=1  OEMID='INTEL '  OEMTableID='EDK2    '  Creator='    '  CreatorRev=0x1000013
bare_metal: A single firmware image writes a consistent OEM ID across every table it produces - an AMI AptioV board is ALASKA/'A M I' throughout. Here WSMT and BGRT are INTEL/'EDK2', the OEM ID that EDK II/OVMF stamps on the tables it builds itself. The split proves two producers: QEMU's generator (rewritten to impersonate AMI, hiding the usual BOCHS/BXPC) and the OVMF firmware underneath (not rewritten). Supporting anomalies: FADT revision 3 where a 2024 AMI UEFI board emits revision 6; a 72-byte SSDT with a 0x20260408 (2026-04-08) iasl compile date where real AMI SSDTs are multi-kilobyte; and only 8 tables total. Confidence: high
repro: Dump ACPI tables with GetSystemFirmwareTable or the Windows ACPI driver and compare the OEMID field (offset 10, 6 bytes) across all tables - any disagreement means mixed producers

title: ACPI table set is missing every AMD platform table a Ryzen/B650 system must publish
evidence:
ACPI tables: MCFG, FACP, APIC, HPET, WSMT, TPM2, SSDT, BGRT
(plus RSDT and DSDT visible under HKLM\HARDWARE\ACPI)
bare_metal: A Ryzen 9000 / B650 platform publishes IVRS (AMD I/O Virtualisation Reporting Structure, for the AMD-Vi IOMMU), CRAT and CDIT (AMD component resource/locality tables), plus the usual FIDT, FPDT, SRAT, SLIT, MSCT, BERT, HEST, EINJ, ERST, PCCT and a dozen vendor SSDTs - typically 25-40 tables. Eight tables, with no AMD-specific table at all, is QEMU's generated q35 set. The presence of RSDT alongside a UEFI boot is a further legacy artefact: modern UEFI firmware exposes XSDT only. Confidence: high (that the AMD tables are mandatory on this platform); medium (exact table counts vary by board)
repro: Enumerate ACPI tables and check for IVRS/CRAT/CDIT on any AMD system; their absence on a claimed AMD platform is disqualifying

command: Get-WmiObject -Namespace root\wmi -Class MSAcpi_ThermalZoneTemperature | Select-Object InstanceName,CurrentTemperature; Get-PhysicalDisk | Get-StorageReliabilityCounter
evidence:

------------            ------------------

DeviceId            : 0
Temperature         : 50
TemperatureMax      : 70
Wear                : 0
PowerOnHours        :
ReadErrorsTotal     :
StartStopCycleCount :
bare_metal: 3000 deciKelvin is exactly 26.85 C - a constant, not a reading; it does not move under load, and 3000 is the hardcoded default in QEMU's ACPI thermal zone. A real B650 board exposes several zones (CPU, chipset, VRM) reporting varying, non-round values. Likewise a genuine Samsung 990 PRO returns a full SMART/health log: PowerOnHours, read/write error counts, start-stop cycles and a live composite temperature. Here those fields are blank and temperature/limit are the flat 50/70 defaults of QEMU's NVMe SMART log. Confidence: high for the thermal constant; high for the empty SMART fields
repro: Read MSAcpi_ThermalZoneTemperature twice under heavy CPU load - a bare-metal zone changes, this one stays at 3000. Then check PowerOnHours on the boot SSD.

title: Max extended CPUID leaf claims 0x80000022 but the SME/SEV leaf 0x8000001F returns all zeros
command: Raw CPUID via VirtualAlloc'd stub, leaves 0x80000000 and 0x8000001F
evidence:
MaxExtLeaf = 0x80000022
Leaf 0x8000001F (SEV/SME): EAX=0x00000000 EBX=0x00000000
bare_metal: Leaf 0x8000001F is within the advertised range (0x1F < 0x22), so a real CPU answering there returns its memory-encryption capabilities: Ryzen 9000 desktop silicon supports SME and sets EAX bit 0, with EBX reporting the C-bit position and the physical-address reduction. Returning all zeros for an in-range leaf means the leaf is not backed by hardware - the hypervisor advertised the host's maximum leaf number while declining to pass through the encryption feature (it cannot, since the guest does not own the memory controller). Confidence: medium - desktop SME reporting varies with firmware, so this is corroborating rather than standalone
repro: Walk every extended CPUID leaf up to the value in 0x80000000:EAX and flag in-range leaves that return all zeros

title: Flat single-bus PCI topology with 8 devices, no PCIe root ports, no AMD data-fabric functions and no IOMMU

evidence:
VEN_8086&DEV_29C0  PCI bus 0, device 0,  function 0
VEN_1234&DEV_1111  PCI bus 0, device 1,  function 0
VEN_144D&DEV_A80C  PCI bus 0, device 3,  function 0
VEN_8086&DEV_10D3  PCI bus 0, device 4,  function 0
VEN_1033&DEV_0194  PCI bus 0, device 6,  function 0
VEN_8086&DEV_2918  PCI bus 0, device 31, function 0
VEN_8086&DEV_2922  PCI bus 0, device 31, function 2
VEN_8086&DEV_2930  PCI bus 0, device 31, function 3

bare_metal: Every Zen-based system exposes the AMD data-fabric/SMN functions at 00:18.0 through 00:18.7 and the AMD-Vi IOMMU at 00:00.2, plus PCIe root ports bridging to buses 01 and up for the M.2 slots, the chipset uplink and the x16 graphics slot - typically 30-60 PCI functions across 5-10 buses. repro: Enumerate PCI location info and check for a bridge to any bus other than 0, and for the 00:18.x functions on any AMD system
